title: A geometrically regular local field algebra is adically formally smooth
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $(B,\mathfrak n)$ be a commutative Noetherian local $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], where $\mathfrak n$ is its unique maximal ideal. Assume that $B$ is geometrically regular over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. Then $k\to B$ is formally smooth for the $\mathfrak n$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]. No finite-type, completeness, characteristic, or separability hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 07EL, theorem-regular-fs, implication (1) implies (2), in characteristic zero and in positive characteristic; in characteristic zero geometric regularity in particular gives regularity by the trivial field extension.

proof.text: Put $K=B/\mathfrak n$. Taking the identity finite purely inseparable extension in [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] shows that $B$ is regular; localizing at its unique maximal ideal leaves $B$ unchanged, so it is regular local. If $\operatorname{char}k=0$, [lem-weil-pbc-perfect-field-separating-basis] applied to every finitely generated intermediate field of $K/k$ shows that $K/k$ is separable, precisely as in [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]. The new lemma [lem-sfb-regular-local-separable-residue-adic-smooth] therefore proves the conclusion in this case.

source.place: Tag 07EL, theorem-regular-fs, characteristic-zero paragraph; Tag 07EJ, lemma-regular-implies-fs.

proof.text: It remains to consider $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$. The node [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-regular-h1-injective] gives regular locality and injectivity of the canonical map $H_1(L_{K/k})\to\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n^2$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-h1-injective-differentials-injective-char-p] with exactly these canonical presentations and residue map yields an injective $K$-linear comparison $\lambda:\Omega_{k/\mathbf F_p}\otimes_k K\to\Omega_{B/\mathbf F_p}\otimes_B K$. These are the modules and universal derivations of [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials].

source.place: Tag 07E5, proposition-characterization-geometrically-regular, (1) implies (3) and (3) implies (4); Tag 07EL, conditions (4) and (5).

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-small-kernel-criterion] for $k\to B$ and $\mathfrak n$. Thus fix a $k$-algebra $D$, an ideal $J$ with $J^2=0$, and a $k$-algebra map $g:B\to D/J$ killing $\mathfrak n^r$, $r\ge1$, and assume that representatives of $g(\mathfrak n)$ annihilate $J$. Multiplication through $g$ makes $J$ a $B$-module: changing a lift changes the product by $J^2=0$. The extra annihilation condition makes it a $K$-vector space. Every element $a\in\mathbf F_p$ satisfies $a^p=a$ (the Frobenius fixes $1$ and hence its sums), so [lem-weil-pbc-perfect-field-separating-basis] and [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension] show that $K/\mathbf F_p$ is separable. Since $B$ is regular local, [lem-sfb-regular-local-separable-residue-adic-smooth] over $\mathbf F_p$ gives a ring map $\psi:B\to D$ lifting $g$ and compatible with $\mathbf F_p$.

source.place: Tag 07EL, theorem-regular-fs, last two paragraphs: reduction to kernels annihilated by the maximal ideal and lifting over the prime field.

proof.text: Write $i:k\to B$ and $\varphi:k\to D$ for the structure maps. The defect $\delta=\psi i-\varphi:k\to J$ is additive and zero on $\mathbf F_p$. Since $J^2=0$, expanding $\psi(i(a))=\varphi(a)+\delta(a)$ gives $\delta(ab)=\varphi(a)\delta(b)+\varphi(b)\delta(a)$. By [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] it factors as a $k$-linear map $\Omega_{k/\mathbf F_p}\to J$, hence as a $K$-linear map $\xi:\Omega_{k/\mathbf F_p}\otimes_kK\to J$, $\xi(\mathrm da\otimes c)=c\delta(a)$. View $\xi$ on the image $P$ of the injection $\lambda$ from step 2. Extend it to $\widetilde\xi:\Omega_{B/\mathbf F_p}\otimes_BK\to J$: if $P$ is the whole space there is nothing to extend; otherwise choose $v\notin P$ and apply [lem-sfb-linear-map-extension-prescribed-value] with prescribed value zero. The composite $\Delta(b)=\widetilde\xi(\mathrm db\otimes1)$ is a derivation $B\to J$ and satisfies $\Delta i=\delta$.

source.place: Tag 07EL, theorem-regular-fs, final paragraph, differential extension of the defect derivation.

proof.text: Set $f=\psi-\Delta$. It is additive and preserves $1$. For $b,c\in B$, the derivation identity and $J^2=0$ give $f(b)f(c)=\psi(b)\psi(c)-\psi(b)\Delta(c)-\psi(c)\Delta(b)=\psi(bc)-\Delta(bc)=f(bc)$; the $B$-action on $J$ is multiplication by any lift under $g$, so it may be computed with $\psi$. Moreover $qf=g$, since $\Delta(B)\subseteq J$, and $fi=\psi i-\delta=\varphi$. This is the required $k$-algebra lift for the reduced test. The small-kernel criterion now proves formal smoothness for all tests in [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]. Explicitly, any resulting lift of a map killing $\mathfrak n^r$ kills $\mathfrak n^{2r}$, because it maps $\mathfrak n^r$ into the square-zero ideal, so the lift is continuous as well.

source.place: Tag 07EL, theorem-regular-fs, final sentence; Tag 07EC, lemma-formally-smooth, continuity of a square-zero lift.

proof_origin.place: Tag 07EL, theorem-regular-fs, characteristic-zero case and (5) implies (2), using Tag 07E5 and Tag 07EJ; the already recorded small-kernel criterion supplies the filtration.
